To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
caffeine pretreatment of BS cells in the first cell cycle, followed by treatment with mitomycin C during second cell cycle, resulted in a significant increase of SCE.

caffeine pretreatment of BS cells, followed by treatment with bifunctional alkylating agents (MC) during the second cycle, produced a synergistic effect in increasing the SCE level, whereas caffeine pretreatment of normal cells, followed by bifunctional alkalyating agents during the second cycle did not increase SCE above the level of the alkylating agents alone.

CAF pretreatment of BS cells in combination with MC or M-MC post-treatment for 2 cell-cycles significantly increases SCE in BS lymphocytes, whereas the combination of CAF with BrdU and MC does not significantly increase SCE in BS cells; and CAF alone does not increase the SCE frequency in either BS cells, or in normal cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the effect of CAF on the frequency of SCE in BS and normal cells, and on chromosome aberrations in normal cells, in order to determine whether CAF is useful in increasing the sensitivity of BS cells in the detection of carcinogens.
the effects of CAF on the SCE frequency and the induction of multiple chromosome aberrations (MCA) in normal and BS lymphocytes.
the mechanism of SCE and the effect of caffeine on SCE and chromosome damage induced by alkylating agents.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the SCE in BS cells are due to the inherent defect in these cells, i.e., a defect of the template strand.
the effect of CAF on SCE is dependent on the nature of the DNA lesion induced.

CAF alone did increase the SCE frequency in normal cells and in BS cells treated with MC or M-MC; however, CAF did not increase SCE in BS cells treated by MC + CAF or M-MC +CAF, nor did it increase the frequency of chromosome aberrations in either BS cells treated with CAF +MC or CAF +M-MC or in normal cells treated with C-AF +M-MC.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the effect of CAF on SCE in BS cells is due to a reduction in DNA-chain growth, and the synergistic SCE-inducing effect of M-MC and CAF is due to the double-stranded lesions in DNA which are induced by M-MC.
CAF in the presence of M-MC or bifunctional alkylating agents increased the SCE rate and chromosome aberrations in both BS and normal cells.
caffeine enhances SCE and chromosome aberration frequencies induced by alkylating agents.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CAF pretreatment of BS cells in combination with alklylating agents (M-MC and MC) significantly increased the SCE frequency.
the effect of CAF on the SCE frequency is not related to the effect of CEF on DNA-chain growth rate.

the combination of M-MC and CAF, as well as MC and CAF, may be useful for the detection of individuals with a genetic predisposition to cancer, since the SCE levels in these individuals may be higher than those in normal individuals.
